meta.name: Daily Reflection Tree
meta.description: An end-of-day deterministic reflection tool walking employees through three psychological axes: Locus (Victim→Victor), Orientation (Entitlement→Contribution), Radius (Self→Altrocentrism).

nodes.text: Good evening. You made it to the end of another day — that's worth something. This conversation will take about 5 minutes. No right answers. Just a chance to see how you actually showed up today. Let's begin.
Before we dig in — one word for today. How would you describe it?
options: Productive
Tough
Mixed
Frustrating
Surprising
answer=Productive|Surprising:A1_Q_WHAT_WORKED
answer=Tough|Frustrating|Mixed:A1_Q_HARD_MOMENT

nodes.text: You said '{A1_OPEN.answer}'. Something clearly clicked. When things went well today, what made them happen?
options: I prepared — I'd thought it through beforehand
I adapted quickly when it wasn't going to plan
The right people showed up and helped
Honestly, it just worked out — timing, luck
answer=I prepared — I'd thought it through beforehand|I adapted quickly when it wasn't going to plan:A1_Q_AGENCY_FOLLOW_INT
answer=The right people showed up and helped|Honestly, it just worked out — timing, luck:A1_Q_AGENCY_FOLLOW_EXT

nodes.text: You said '{A1_OPEN.answer}'. Those days carry weight. When something didn't go to plan, what was your first instinct?
options: Figure out what I could still control in the situation
Wait and see if things resolved themselves
Feel frustrated that others hadn't done their part
Push through on my own without asking for help
answer=Figure out what I could still control in the situation|Push through on my own without asking for help:A1_Q_AGENCY_FOLLOW_INT
answer=Wait and see if things resolved themselves|Feel frustrated that others hadn't done their part:A1_Q_AGENCY_FOLLOW_EXT

nodes.text: At some point today, something didn't go your way. What did you do with that moment?
options: I made a decision — not a perfect one, but mine
I named the problem clearly and communicated it
I changed my approach mid-stream
I let it pass and moved to the next thing

nodes.text: Looking back at that difficult moment — somewhere in it, even small, was there a choice that was yours to make?
options: Yes — I see it now, even if I didn't act on it
Maybe — it's hard to see in the moment
Not really — the situation didn't leave room
I'm not sure — I'd need to think more
signal=axis1:internal:A1_R_INTERNAL
signal=axis1:external:A1_R_EXTERNAL

nodes.text: You kept your hand on the wheel today — even when the road wasn't smooth. That's not nothing. Agency isn't about controlling outcomes. It's about staying in the conversation with your own choices. You did that.

Tough days make it easy to feel like things are happening *to* you — and sometimes they genuinely are. But somewhere in '{A1_OPEN.answer}', there was a moment you navigated. Even a small choice counts. Worth sitting with.
Okay. We've looked at how you *handled* things. Now let's look at what you *gave* — and what you were looking to receive.
Think of one interaction you had today — a conversation, a handoff, a meeting. Which of these feels most honest?
options: I gave something — time, knowledge, effort — without being asked
I did what was asked of me, nothing more, nothing less
I was looking for recognition for something I'd already done
I felt that others weren't contributing as much as I was
answer=I gave something — time, knowledge, effort — without being asked|I did what was asked of me, nothing more, nothing less:A2_Q_CONTRIB_FOLLOW
answer=I was looking for recognition for something I'd already done|I felt that others weren't contributing as much as I was:A2_Q_ENTITLE_FOLLOW

nodes.text: When you gave that time or effort today — what was underneath it?
options: It needed to be done and I was the one who could do it
I wanted that person to succeed
It was part of my job — I didn't really think about it
I expected it to be noticed and appreciated
answer=It needed to be done and I was the one who could do it|I wanted that person to succeed:A2_R_CONTRIBUTION
answer=It was part of my job — I didn't really think about it|I expected it to be noticed and appreciated:A2_R_MIXED

nodes.text: That feeling of not getting what you deserved — where did it sit most?
options: Credit for something I worked hard on wasn't acknowledged
I was passed over for something I felt I'd earned
Others got more visibility for less effort
I just felt invisible today

answer=Credit for something I worked hard on wasn't acknowledged|I was passed over for something I felt I'd earned|Others got more visibility for less effort|I just felt invisible today:A2_R_ENTITLEMENT

nodes.text: You gave something today that didn't have your name on it. That kind of contribution is easy to overlook — in yourself and in others. It's also what actually moves things forward. Notice it.

Some of what you gave today was genuine — and some of it was quiet accounting. That's honest. The question worth sitting with: was the giving the point, or was the recognition? No judgment — just worth knowing.

Wanting to be seen for what you've done is human. It becomes a problem when it crowds out noticing what others need. Today you were focused on the ledger — what you were owed. That's worth examining, not because it's wrong, but because it's expensive. Entitlement closes the loop inward.
Last stretch. We've looked at agency and contribution. Now let's zoom out — past you, past your team — and see who else was in the picture today.
When you think about your biggest challenge or moment today — who was in the frame when you thought about it?
options: Mostly me — my workload, my stress, my goals
My immediate team — we were in it together
A specific colleague who I noticed was struggling
The people our work ultimately reaches — customers, users, the end goal
answer=Mostly me — my workload, my stress, my goals:A3_Q_SELF_FOLLOW
answer=My immediate team — we were in it together|A specific colleague who I noticed was struggling:A3_Q_TEAM_FOLLOW
answer=The people our work ultimately reaches — customers, users, the end goal:A3_Q_WIDE_FOLLOW

nodes.text: There's nothing wrong with attending to your own experience. But let's push one layer out — was there anyone today whose situation you paused to consider, even briefly?
options: Yes — a colleague who seemed overwhelmed
Yes — I thought about whether my work was actually useful to someone
Not really — today demanded everything I had
I didn't have the bandwidth for it

nodes.text: You had others in mind today. When you noticed a colleague struggling or the team under pressure — what did you do with that awareness?
options: I stepped in and helped — tangibly
I said something — checked in, acknowledged it
I noticed but stayed focused on my own piece
I felt it, but didn't know what to do

nodes.text: You connected your work today to something beyond the immediate task. What made that connection feel real?
options: I saw the direct impact — a user, a result, feedback
I reminded myself of the why — even when the day was hard
It was more abstract — I know it matters, even if I can't see it
Someone else pointed it out and it landed
signal=axis3:self:A3_R_SELF
signal=axis3:team:A3_R_TEAM
signal=axis3:altrocentric:A3_R_WIDE

nodes.text: Some days we're fully occupied by our own survival. That's real. But Maslow argued — and he was right — that meaning lives on the other side of self-focus. Even one small act of noticing someone else today would have shifted the frame. Tomorrow is a new chance to widen the lens.

You kept others in view today — and that's not automatic. Most people lose peripheral vision when under pressure. The fact that you noticed, and perhaps even acted, is the beginning of what Maslow called self-transcendence: contribution that extends beyond the self.

Connecting today's work to the people it ultimately serves is rare and powerful. When the task itself is the meaning, effort becomes sustainable. You did that today — consciously or not. That's a wider radius than most people operate from.

axis1.internal: You stayed in the driver's seat — or at least kept your hand near the wheel.
axis1.external: The day pulled your attention outward. Worth asking where your choice lived.

axis2.contribution: You were in giving mode — and it showed.
axis2.entitlement: You were tracking the ledger. That's worth examining.

axis3.self: Your frame was tight today — mostly you. Understandable. Worth expanding tomorrow.
axis3.team: You kept others in view. That's not nothing.
axis3.altrocentric: You connected your work to something beyond it. That's a wide lens.

closingInsights: internal+contribution+altrocentric: Three for three. You showed up as the kind of person teams are lucky to have. Don't forget to notice that.
internal+contribution+self: You acted. You gave. But you were still largely in your own orbit. Tomorrow — who else is in the room?
internal+entitlement+team: You stayed in control of your choices, and you kept others in view. But you were also tracking what you deserved. That tension is worth sitting with.
external+contribution+altrocentric: You may not have felt in control today — but you gave, and you were thinking about others. Agency can come back. The orientation was already right.
external+entitlement+self: Today was hard. You felt reactive, you wanted recognition, and the frame was tight. That's an honest day. Tomorrow you get to choose one thing differently.
default: Every day is data. What does today tell you about tomorrow?

nodes.text: That's it for tonight. Same time tomorrow — and you'll have another chance to show up however you choose.
